must_catch.item: The real trigger is the CFO's month-end close, not the portal.
No dollar figure is stated. The rep doesn't know it.
The global/infrastructure opener is reported as silence.

fails: Decider insight claims the team 'never got the CFO into the room'. This is false: Ines attended the reconciliation demo ('go back') and the value-analysis meeting.
Close labels the exact ROI figure and the distributor reference as 'dodged'. The rep openly said he doesn't remember the figure and stated plainly 'We never got her a call', so neither was dodged.
Rep takeaway adds 'Don't cite a dollar figure you can't reproduce'. Nothing in the transcript says the rep cited a figure, so this lesson is unsupported.
data.notes: Strong on the essentials: the report finds the CFO's month-end close as the real trigger, keeps Fiserv's pitch unknown, avoids stating any dollar figure, and reports the infrastructure opener as silence. It misses the named-contact request as a sign of a weak bank relationship. It also leaves out the 60-hours-across-two-people analysis and the developer-story silence from the decided and message sections, and it muddies the decided insight by calling the value figure unreliable when it is what turned the deal from dead to won.
